subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add a core sub-agent `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` lifecycle contract across embedded runtime, gateway wait/session projection, and SDK normalization?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but the proposed remedy changes core event semantics and compatibility expectations across multiple consumers, which needs maintainer direction before automation opens another fix PR.

options.title: Accept the lifecycle contract
options.body: Implement the requested phases on current main, wire consumers intentionally, add docs and focused startup-failure proof, and replace or repair the stale candidate PR as needed.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics or recovery
options.body: Keep the current lifecycle event set and instead add targeted diagnostics, timeout classification, or watchdog recovery for silent startup aborts.

options.title: Decline core event expansion
options.body: Close this issue and the candidate PR with a maintainer rationale if the added event surface is not wanted in core.

recommendation.title: Accept the lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Implement the requested phases on current main, wire consumers intentionally, add docs and focused startup-failure proof, and replace or repair the stale candidate PR as needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and older history put the central lifecycle/gateway projection surfaces under this routing path, and the decision is a core event-contract choice.
